verdictStatement: Both of my v2 blockers and both of my v2 SHOULD-FIX items are genuinely repaired, and I verified each at primary bytes rather than at the repair roster's description of itself. The B-1 attribution split is the real thing: the artifact now states the full-width no-lock rule as its OWN proposal, names the accepted schemas.v2's narrower holding correctly, and denies lending D-013's acceptance to the widening — in three separate places, none of which contradicts another. The change roster is now complete and precise against a whole-key diff. What withholds acceptance is narrower and lives entirely inside the S-2 repair itself: of the eleven newly-digested sources, two carry roles that are false at review time. The schemas.v7 entry asserts currency that v8 has taken, and the delivery.v4 entry offers as the warrant for 'applied' a document whose own bytes read 'NOT APPLIED'. Neither defect touches a rule, an authority, or a window. Both are one-line fixes in the field the v3 delta exists to repair, which is exactly why they should be fixed before this is sealed rather than after.

So the subject's actual proposition — that unaccepted schema successors write the wider rule — survives the head moving. Nothing about the lock rule is wrong.

shouldFix.whyItStillMatters: This lane treats schema-citation currency as a tested property: v2's own repair roster is 'REPOINT citation from … schemas.v3 to schemas.v6 under review', and at the v2 review I explicitly verified that v6 was the head and no v7 existed. v3 makes the same class of claim and it is false at review time. A coordinator using this entry to find the live schema artifact is sent to a superseded one and told its review is pending when it is finished. The exposure is also self-inflicted: the artifact's argument needs only 'an unaccepted successor writes the wider rule' — the words 'Current' and 'under independent review' add nothing it relies on and are the only part that can rot.

I record it as SHOULD-FIX because the claim is falsifiable, false as measured, and one word to fix; a coordinator who judges the race excusing may downgrade it. I do not treat it as a blocker: it lends no acceptance, grants no authority, and changes no rule.

advisories.title: The roster names a path that no longer exists under that name, and never names the metadata class Codex asked to see classified
advisories.detail: basedOn.method lists 'honestyRepairsFromV1' among the repaired paths, but v3 contains no such key — it was RENAMED to honestyRepairsFromV1Historical (contents byte-identical, which I verified). A reviewer resolving the roster path-by-path finds nothing at /honestyRepairsFromV1. Separately, honestyRepairsFromV2[1] claims the roster names 'every v2-to-v3 substantive path', and the word 'substantive' is doing the work of excluding artifact, version, basedOn and honestyRepairsFromV2 itself — but the artifact never says which paths it considers metadata. That is the second half of Codex's CMCV2-S1 requiredRepair ('Keep ordinary succession metadata … clearly classified as metadata so the next reviewer can reproduce a closed path roster') and it is only implied.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: I reproduced the closed roster without difficulty and found no undisclosed substantive change. The property Codex asked for holds; only its statement is implicit. Recorded so the next successor can close it cheaply, not as a bar to acceptance.
advisories.suggestedFix: Write 'honestyRepairsFromV1 → honestyRepairsFromV1Historical (renamed, contents unchanged)' in the roster, and add one clause naming artifact/version/basedOn/honestyRepairsFromV2 as succession metadata outside the substantive roster.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the attribution repair was cosmetic — that lockJoin's rule text was quietly widened or narrowed under cover of an 'attribution only' label. Refuted by string decomposition: the v2 rule text and closing sentence survive byte-identical.
That the S-STATE repair swapped one unwarranted vocabulary for another. Refuted: the replacement concepts are the DR-124 row's own words at file 08 L306.
That the S-2 repair padded governingSources with sources it does not actually use. Each of the eleven new entries maps to a specific claim in the artifact, and I traced all of them.

That doctor-contract.v4 being D-035-accepted for DR-114 lets the subject admit S-DOCTOR by the back door. It does not — the entry accepts the DR-114 standing and refuses the DR-111 row in the same sentence.
That 'D-015 T-3' was a decorative citation carried unexamined from v1. It is not: T-3 in D-015's accepted subject is precisely the bridges-versus-translation tension.

That S-ROLE RESERVED plus S-EVIDENCE DEFERRED means the artifact cannot close a row whose acceptance cell demands per-surface matrices. Disclosed rather than smuggled, and DR202-RR-F3's routed remedy is exactly a D-002-style scoped closure. Unchanged from my v2 assessment.
That some residual site still lends D-013's acceptance to the full-width rule. Eleven-occurrence sweep of 'accepted': none does.
coordinatorNote: This is a good-faith successor and it repairs what it claims to repair — I want that on the record plainly, because the verdict word alone will understate it. Both of my v2 blockers are gone at the bytes, not merely at the roster, and the S-1 restatement is better than the minimum I asked for. The two SHOULD-FIX items are the same species as each other and both sit inside the S-2 repair: a role sentence that was true when written and is false now (schemas.v7 'Current'), and a role sentence that names the wrong document as its warrant (delivery.v4 'applied'). Neither touches a rule, an authority, a window, or an acceptance. Both are one-line edits. If the coordinator judges the v8 race as excusing S-1, S-2 still stands on its own and the gate is still 0-and-0. DR-111 remains OPEN. Nothing here marks it SATISFIED and no implementation is authorized.
